entries.what_happened: Three manuscripts in the family bear on this. (1) 'A counterexample to Hadwiger's conjecture' (folder A-counterexample-to-Hadwigers-conjecture-September-23-2026) proves Theorem 1.1: for arbitrarily large m there are m-vertex finite simple graphs G with independence number alpha(G) <= 2 and cm(G) < m/100, where cm(G) is the largest connected matching (disjoint edges, every two of which are joined by an edge between their endpoint sets). Its Proposition 'matching-minor' proves that every finite graph has h(G) <= (m + 4 cm(G) + 2)/3, and since every colour class has at most two vertices, chi(G) >= m/2. For the constructed graphs this gives h(G) < 26m/75 + 2/3 < m/2 <= chi_f(G) <= chi(G) (Corollary 1.2), so chi(G) > h(G) and chi_f(G) > h(G). (2) 'A counterexample to the Colin de Verdiere chromatic conjecture' (folder A-counterexample-to-the-Colin-de-Verdiere-chromatic-conjecture-September-23-2026) builds, by a separate route, clique blow-ups H[s] of sampled base graphs H with alpha <= 2, and proves mu(G) + 1 < |V(G)|/2 <= chi(G). Its fractional-colouring corollary chains chi_f >= |V|/2 > kappa + 1 >= mu + 1 >= h, and the manuscript itself says these graphs also violate Hadwiger's inequality. The step mu + 1 >= h is the classical minor-monotonicity inequality, cited to van der Holst, Lovasz and Schrijver rather than proved there. (3) 'A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number' (folder A-linear-list-coloring-bound-in-terms-of-the-Hadwiger-number-September-23-2026) proves list-chi(G) <= C h(G) for an absolute integer C, hence chi(G) <= C h(G) by a common list. This is a linear-coefficient statement; it is not chi <= h and does not assert it.
entries.delivers: If correct, it disproves the conjecture as the list states it: the list asks for chi(G) <= h(G) for every loopless graph, and the manuscript states the conjecture for finite nonempty simple graphs. Its counterexamples are simple and hence loopless, so the disproof transfers to the list's wording. The colouring form (2) also fails: for a counterexample G with h = h(G), take t = h + 1; G has no K_t minor and chi(G) >= t, so G is not (t-1)-colourable. The failure is not confined to small t: the examples are arbitrarily large, with h(G) below 26m/75 + 2/3 (about 0.35m) and chi(G) >= m/2. The same graphs also disprove the Reed-Seymour fractional weakening (fractional chi <= h), which the list does not ask about. Restrictions: the examples have independence number at most two; there are no restrictions on the scope of the disproof itself, since one counterexample suffices for a universal statement. The manuscript does not say the result settles the problem in so many words, but its abstract says 'We disprove Hadwiger's conjecture'.
entries.remains: If the claim holds, neither problem_asks (1) nor (2) remains open, since both the universal inequality and its colouring form are false. Variants the list excludes (linear, asymptotic, odd, or restricted-class forms) are not decided by these manuscripts, except that the list manuscript proves a linear-coefficient bound chi <= C h with an absolute C, which is a different statement from the one asked.
entries.direction: disproves the conjecture (chromatic and colouring forms), and also its fractional weakening
entries.object: No explicit object. The graphs are random samples: the Hadwiger manuscript builds them by sampling positions from a finite probability space, with holes fixed by an algebraic tensor/frame relation, and shows the sample has the required properties with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(m)) (Proposition 'raw-to-graph'). Existence is therefore probabilistic, not explicit. The Colin manuscript's graphs are clique blow-ups of such sampled base graphs and have the same status.
entries.doubts: I found no sketch flags, hedges, or deferral phrases bearing on the main argument in the three manuscripts (a search for sketch, omitted, routine, analogous, and similar wording found only local remarks). Scope of my reading: the probabilistic core (Theorem 'raw-supersaturation') is spread across roughly a dozen sections. I read its statement, the graph-deduction proposition, the matching-count proposition (its proof and arithmetic, including 26/75 and 2/3), and the completion argument. The completion argument invokes earlier propositions (status preparation, positive overlap, rare overlap) for its overlap inputs, and I did not check those inputs, so the step-level correctness of the core is not assessed here.

entries.not_relevant_because: The list manuscript (A linear list-coloring bound in terms of the Hadwiger number) bounds the list chromatic number of vertices by a multiple of the Hadwiger number, and none of the three manuscripts mentions edge colourings, the chromatic index, the list chromatic index of edges, or line graphs (checked by search), so nothing in the family bears on whether ch'(G) = chi'(G) for edges.
